skill.name: parallel-task-spark
skill.description: Coordinates dependency-aware development tasks across parallel Sparky subagents, validates each result, commits task changes, and updates the source plan.
skill.summary: Execute a markdown development plan in validated parallel waves.

content.value_statement: Large development plans are slow when independent tasks run sequentially. This skill schedules ready tasks in parallel, validates results, commits changes, and updates plan logs.
actual_capabilities: Reads markdown plans and extracts task identifiers, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and validation steps.
Filters requested task subsets while retaining required dependencies.
Launches all unblocked tasks in parallel waves with the Sparky agent role.
Requires RED-to-GREEN test evidence or a documented alternative verification method.
Reviews completed work and retries or escalates unsuccessful tasks.
Commits task changes locally and records status, files, and work logs in the plan.
limitations: Requires a structured markdown plan with recognizable task sections and dependency metadata.
Depends on an environment that supports Sparky and test-writer subagents.
Modifies repository files, creates local commits, and edits the selected plan.
Never pushes commits and only runs after an explicit command.

use_cases.title: Parallel Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Run independent implementation tasks together while preserving dependency order and task-level validation.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers implementing a structured feature plan

use_cases.title: Coordinated Refactoring
use_cases.description: Divide a refactoring plan into safe waves with focused commits and recorded outcomes.

use_cases.title: Test-Guided Implementation
use_cases.description: Require failing tests before implementation and passing evidence before each task is complete.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Run /parallel-task-spark plans/profile-plan.md and complete every task in dependency order.
prompt_templates.scenario: Execute a small prepared plan with default behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Run Selected Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Run /parallel-task-spark plans/auth-plan.md for tasks T1, T2, and T4, including their required dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Complete only a selected part of a larger plan.

prompt_templates.title: Enforce Verification Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute /parallel-task-spark plans/migration-plan.md and require RED-to-GREEN evidence or a documented alternative for every task.
prompt_templates.scenario: Apply strict validation requirements across parallel task waves.

prompt_templates.title: Complete and Audit a Release Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute /parallel-task-spark plans/release-plan.md in dependency waves, confirm local commits, update each task log, and report unresolved issues.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate a complex plan with complete execution records.

output_examples.input: Run the complete user profile plan.
output: Assigned three ready tasks in the first wave and two dependent tasks in the second wave.
Validated each task with test evidence and local commits.
Updated the plan with completion logs, modified files, and remaining issues.

output_examples.input: Run tasks T3 and T7 from the authentication plan.
output_examples.output: Included required dependencies, completed available tasks in waves, recorded verification evidence, and reported one blocked task with its next step.

best_practices: Use stable, unique task identifiers and explicit dependency lists in every plan.
Include acceptance criteria and exact validation commands for each task.
Review local commits and plan logs before starting the next wave.
anti_patterns: Do not invoke the skill on an unstructured document without clear task sections.
Do not assign overlapping files to parallel tasks without coordination.
Do not expect remote pushes; the workflow creates local commits only.

faq.question: What plan format does this skill require?
faq.answer: Use markdown task headings with unique identifiers, dependency lists, descriptions, acceptance criteria, and validation steps.

faq.question: Can I run only selected tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide task identifiers, and the skill also includes their required dependencies.

faq.question: How are task dependencies handled?
faq.answer: Tasks run only after every listed dependency is complete. Newly unblocked tasks start in the next parallel wave.

faq.question: What happens when a task has no suitable tests?
faq.answer: The task must record why tests are unsuitable and provide exact manual, static, or runtime verification.

faq.question: Does the skill push commits to a remote repository?
faq.answer: No. It creates local task commits and explicitly prohibits pushing them.

faq.question: Which subagent roles does the workflow use?
faq.answer: Implementation tasks require the Sparky role. Testable tasks also use a test-writer subagent for the initial failing tests.
